mappings.note: Unscramble the resource names, then sort them as renewable or non-renewable. The sorting is the marked work, LO-120.
Hold your breath, time it, and report how it feels. A first-person investigation with an observation to record, LO-121.
Compare soil samples by naked eye and under a lens, recording colour and texture. LO-121 for the guided observation, LO-118 because the record is of appearance and texture, LO-118's own register.
Cut, fold and pin a firki, then explain that moving air turns it. LO-126 is construct a model from surrounding materials and explain its working, exactly this.
Four true/false claims about what counts as a natural resource and which are renewable. Sorting resources into the chapter's classes, LO-120.
Petrol as the fuel for two-wheelers. Matching a resource to its everyday use, LO-127.
Which of coal, water, natural gas and petrol is renewable -- water. Sorting resources by renewability, LO-120. This row duplicates the previous item's stem with its answer text appended.
Classify coal, natural gas, forests and minerals. Sorting resources by renewability, LO-120.
WHY petroleum is non-renewable -- formed over millions of years, used far faster. The item asks for the cause behind the label, LO-122.
Justify that forests are hard to regrow -- slow trees, eroded soil, lost seed, changed climate. A chain of causes, LO-122.
List five daily activities using natural resources and how to use less. LO-128 names minimising the wastage of water and electricity as its own example.
Same reduce-your-use task as the preceding item, whose answer has been concatenated into this stem; the printed answer belongs to a wind-farm question. Mapped on the stem, LO-128.
What windmills are for -- flour mills, pumping water, generating electricity. A resource put to work, LO-127.
What saline water is. Identifying a material by an observable property, LO-118.
About two-thirds of Earth's surface is water. A quantity attached to a resource, LO-124.
The main DIFFERENCE between saline water and freshwater for domestic use. An explicit differentiation on a property, LO-119.
Which activity pollutes water -- dumping household and industrial waste. A cause of a degraded resource, LO-122, the frame's own 'quality with pollutants' pattern.
The purpose of rainwater harvesting. LO-128 names rainwater harvesting explicitly.
Is large-scale felling for industry and housing justified? Prepare a report. An argued case for protecting the environment, LO-128.
Propose a plan to cut the school's water use and say how to make it happen. LO-128 for the conservation aim, LO-129 because designing and planning the scheme is the student's own creative work.
What natural resources are. Identifying the category the chapter works with, LO-118.
Oxygen is about 21% of air. A quantity in the composition of air, LO-124.
Why air is essential -- oxygen drives respiration. Explaining a process, LO-123.
Wind is moving air. Naming a phenomenon by its observable character, LO-118.
Four activities air makes possible -- breathing, flight, burning, windmills. Resources put to work in daily life, LO-127.
List actions to raise the green cover of your locality. LO-128 names caring for plants and spreading awareness.
Identify solar cooking and give one benefit and one drawback. Judging an energy choice in daily life, LO-127.
Why large-scale felling damages soil -- roots no longer bind it, so it erodes. A cause-and-effect chain, LO-122.
Two ways humans pollute air (LO-122, air quality related to pollutants, the LO's own example) plus one action to reduce it (LO-128).
What happens to a solar-panel, gas-stove and windmill household after a sunless week. Reasoning about a real energy mix, LO-127.

Fill blanks with fossil fuels, forest, air, petroleum, coal, water and non-renewable resource. Sorting resources into the chapter's classes, LO-120. The printed answer belongs to a different item, about bawadis and vavs.
The Sun is Earth's main energy source. Naming the resource, LO-118.
How the Sun indirectly feeds a grazing cow -- photosynthesis then consumption. A chain of causes traced back, LO-122.
Rooftop panels capturing sunlight are solar panels. A resource put to work at home, LO-127.
What a forest is -- a large area of dense, varied plant growth. Identification by observable features, LO-118.
Van Mahotsav, the July tree-planting week. Efforts to protect the environment and spread awareness, LO-128.
How forest roots hold soil against erosion. A structure related to its effect, LO-122.
How soil forms -- rock disintegrating under sun, water and organisms over long time. Explaining a process, LO-123.
Which are fossil fuels -- petroleum, natural gas, coal. Sorting resources into a class, LO-120.
Why they are called fossil fuels -- formed from buried ancient organisms under heat and pressure. Explaining the process of formation, LO-123.
What renewable resources are. Defining a class, LO-120.
The main DIFFERENCE between renewable and non-renewable resources. An explicit differentiation on rate of replenishment, LO-119.
Coal as the non-renewable one. Placing a resource in a class, LO-120.
Which action conserves fossil fuels -- public transport or cycling. A protective habit, LO-128.
Assertion-reason: the Sun is the main energy source BECAUSE energy flows from plants through the food chain. The causal clause is what is marked, LO-122.
A community storing rooftop rainwater for the dry season. LO-128's own rainwater-harvesting example.
CNG is Compressed Natural Gas. Naming a material, LO-118.
Why resources must be used judiciously -- meeting present needs without harming the future. The argument that grounds LO-128.
Rock breaking down over long time is disintegration or weathering. Naming a process, LO-123.
Which metals come from minerals -- aluminium, gold, copper, iron. Identifying materials, LO-118.
Why village air differs from city air -- vehicle smoke and pollution. Air quality related to pollutants, LO-122's own example.
Which is NOT a windmill use -- making building materials. Tests the real applications of a resource, LO-127.
Windmill farms run on wind energy. A resource put to work at scale, LO-127.
Assertion-reason on forests being important because they shelter wildlife, hold soil and supply products. The case for protecting forests, LO-128.
Electric vehicles as a shift toward renewable energy. A city-level measure to reduce fossil-fuel use, LO-128.
Nitrogen is about 78% of air. A quantity in the composition of air, LO-124.
Why restoring a forest takes years -- slow trees and a complex interdependent ecosystem. A chain of causes, LO-122.
Limited resources that are not replenished are non-renewable. Defining a class, LO-120.
Air temperature as the weather parameter behind forecasts. A measured physical quantity, LO-124.
Why electric vehicles pollute less -- no tailpipe smoke. Air quality related to its pollutants, LO-122's own example.
